title: R3 falsification — the shipped renderer leaks tenant theme tokens to the document root
description: Measured in the running app before the shell's workaround was added. FormspecProvider calls emitThemeTokens(themeDocument.tokens) with no target; that helper defaults to document.documentElement and has no unmount cleanup. Once the intake route renders once, the tenant's brand colour is an inline custom property on <html> for the life of the page.
defectLocation: formspec/packages/formspec-react/src/context.tsx — FormspecProvider useEffect calling emitThemeTokens(themeDocument.tokens) with no target; emitThemeTokens defaults to document.documentElement
whyItMatters: THEME-ROUTE-CLASS's runtime guarantee cannot be honoured by a host from outside. The shell's boundary is structurally correct — nothing tenant-shaped crosses into a refusing route's props or subtree — and is defeated anyway by a global side effect inside the renderer it composes with.

measurementBeforeWorkaround.step: fresh page load directly on /certify (ceremony, refuses)
navigate to /apply (intake, admits) — the shipped renderer mounts

measurementBeforeWorkaround.verdict: LEAKED — the tenant token is still in the cascade on a route whose class refuses tenant theming

whyNothingLooksWrong: The refusing routes in this bundle contain no shipped Formspec components, and the shell's own chrome reads no --formspec-color-* property.

correction.struck: Put a definition-form slot on a proof route — schema-valid, nothing forbids it — and the receipt renders in the tenant's brand.
correction.why: Falsified by this spike's own app. The measurement steps above are unchanged; only this interpretive sentence was wrong. A definition-form slot on a proof route IS schema-valid and nothing forbids it, but it would not paint the receipt in the tenant's brand: the shell hands that slot the refusing route's grant, so FormspecProvider re-emits the 45 platform tokens over the leaked ones on <html> and FormspecForm writes the platform values inline on its own container, where they beat anything inherited. Independently, r2-theme-reaches-but-paints-nothing.json measured zero elements painting with the brand token even where it does resolve.
correction.correctedExposure: The defect is the unscoped global write, not what a route contains. It outlives the component that made it, a host can only clean up after it rather than prevent it, and it reaches everything outside a .formspec-container — host chrome, portalled content, a second embedded renderer, any future skin that does paint the brand token.

measurement.how: Driven with Playwright against the static build (http://localhost:4174/apply), reading getComputedStyle --formspec-color-primary. The shipped renderer is mounted and untouched; only the two inline emissions are set, to reproduce the shape a definition-form slot on a proof route would produce.

asShipped.note: intake route, tenant theme admitted — both agree, so this case cannot distinguish which one wins

rootOverwrittenWithPlatformValue.note: a write to <html> does not reach into a container that emitted its own value

proofRouteShape.verdict: PLATFORM. With the tenant token leaked on <html> and the platform grant emitted inline on the form's own container, the form and every field inside it resolve the PLATFORM brand value. The leaked token does not reach them.

measurement.whyTheGrantIsPlatformThere: resolveThemeGrant returns a ThemeDocument built from buildPlatformTheme() on every refusing class (45 tokens, color.primary #27594f), and that is the only theme any slot renderer on that route receives. FormspecProvider emits those 45 to <html>, overwriting the leaked values; FormspecForm emits them inline on its own container, which is what the measurement above reproduces.

workaround: src/theme-grant.ts enforceDocumentRootThemeBoundary — the shell scrubs --formspec-* off <html> whenever a refusing route renders. Recorded in the gap ledger as renderer-emits-tenant-tokens-to-document-root. The fix belongs in formspec-react: scope the emission to the component's own container, which FormspecForm already does correctly and with cleanup.
